DC-300 suction motor: recurring failure is usually caused by a clogged filter; check and replace the filter on every service to prevent repeats.
Main machine warranty is 2 years from installation; components are 1 year. The suction motor is treated as a component, so it is out of warranty after the first year.

How to check a unit's warranty: find its sales invoice for the purchase date; the main machine is covered for 2 years and components for 1 year. A unit past those dates is out of warranty and its repairs are billable.

Spare parts stocked in the warehouse include suction motors, hydraulic seals, footcovers, water hoses, and handpieces. A spare-part stockout is the main cause of a long wait between a reported fault and the repair.
A spare part typically ships in 7 to 17 days across the archipelago; when the warehouse is out of stock, that lead time is the top cause of the wait between a reported fault and its repair.
DC-300 units tend to fail close to their warranty end date. Review a DC-300 before a renewal so a repair that is about to become billable is not wrongly honoured as warranty.
A new dental unit is installed on-site, then covered by scheduled preventive maintenance. After installation, technicians also run basic training for the clinic's staff on daily care and cleaning.

How long is the warranty on a dental unit? The main machine is covered for 2 years from installation, and its components for 1 year. After that the unit is out of warranty and its repairs are billable.
How often is preventive maintenance? It is scheduled automatically every six months, from installation or the last maintenance, with reminders at H-30, H-14, and H-7 before it is due.
When do warranty reminders fire? At H-90, H-30, and H-7 before the warranty ends. Warranty status shows as in-warranty, nearing end, ended, or not applicable on every ticket.
Troubleshooting suction motor failure: the usual root cause is a clogged suction filter. Inspect and replace the suction motor to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting hydraulic leak on the chair: the usual root cause is a worn hydraulic seal. Inspect and replace the hydraulic seal to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting footcover cracked: the usual root cause is material fatigue on the footcover. Inspect and replace the footcover to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting low-speed water hose misrouted: the usual root cause is a split low-speed water hose. Inspect and replace the water hose to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting panoramic adaptor dead: the usual root cause is a failed S60 panoramic adaptor. Inspect and replace the panoramic adaptor to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting compressor overheating: the usual root cause is a blocked compressor filter. Inspect and replace the compressor filter to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting handpiece not spinning: the usual root cause is worn handpiece bearings. Inspect and replace the handpiece to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting LED operatory light out: the usual root cause is a failed LED light module. Inspect and replace the LED light module to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting foot pedal unresponsive: the usual root cause is a worn foot-pedal switch. Inspect and replace the foot pedal to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting air compressor pressure drop: the usual root cause is a leaking compressor pressure valve. Inspect and replace the compressor pressure valve to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting x-ray sensor miscalibrated: the usual root cause is an x-ray sensor out of calibration. Inspect and replace the x-ray sensor to prevent a repeat visit.
Troubleshooting autoclave not sealing: the usual root cause is a perished autoclave door gasket. Inspect and replace the autoclave gasket to prevent a repeat visit.
